newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus profits fall on narrowing margins.
newsitem.headline: Fokus profits fall on narrowing margins.

text.p: Norway's third largest commercial bank, Fokus Bank, on Thursday reported nine-month net profits fell to 383 million ($60 million) from 416 million in the corresponding year-ago period.

The bank attributed the weaker result to narrowing interest margins, which are a result of the competitive situation in Norway's overbanked financial market as well as a generally lower risk of new loans.
But Fokus said the lower interest margin was partly offset by reduced operating expenses.
Total operating expenses were trimmed to 620 million crowns from 649 million in the nine-month period in 1995.
"This shows that the bank is able to meet the increased competition by improved effectiveness," a statement said.

Net interest income, the bank's core business, fell to 689 million crowns from 730 million. Total other operating income decreased by three million crowns to 330 million because of reduced real estate exposure and lower contribution from associated companies.

The operating result before losses shrank to 399 million from 414 million. The pre-tax result fell to 393 million from 416 million. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast a pre-tax result of 385 million crowns.
The group's total assets increased by 4.9 billion crowns compared to the same time last year, of which three billion crowns is lending growth. This represents a lending growth of 11.9 percent.
